A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, mathematical statements, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical bounds, an explicit maxout construction, and mathematical proofs. The computational proof discussed in the introduction belongs to prior work; Remark 6.3 suggests a possible computer check without reporting original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: V2 retains the theoretical contributions and appendices without adding experiments, simulations, or data analyses. The newly discussed results are attributed to other research.

M1.justification: The network definitions, conforming-network framework, and explicit rank-(3,2) maxout construction remain unchanged. Proposition 6.1 uses the same functions and coefficients; revisions to theoretical coverage do not introduce a different computational procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical training or evaluation tasks. The mathematical maximum-function examples remain the same.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates experimental comparators. Newly cited theoretical results change research positioning, not membership in an evaluated baseline comparison.

E3.justification: Neither version reports empirical evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses appear in either version. The dimension-four argument, explicit maxout example, and appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. The explicit maxout construction and its Appendix B calculation yielding −2 are unchanged; revisions to formal mathematical statements are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: The main theorems and proofs remain essentially unchanged. V1's general-rank maxout Corollary 4.9 is no longer stated, although its derivation survives in v2 Appendix B without the former definition of R. V2 also removes Conjecture 1.1, changes the quoted N-ary-weight bound from Ω(log N / log log d) to Ω(log d / log log N), and omits the σ_M factor from the inverse formula in Proposition 2.3 that appeared in v1 Proposition 2.4.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the same three headline contributions. However, v2's introduction no longer claims the lower-bound extension to arbitrary maxout rank vectors, modestly narrowing the advertised contribution scope while retaining the ReLU bound and seven-number maxout construction.

C2.justification: V1 motivates braid-conformity through cancellation of extraneous breakpoints and suggests progress toward Conjecture 1.1. V2 removes that rationale and adds Section 7, explaining that the cited unrestricted two-layer representation of the five-number maximum makes conformity a real restriction; it explicitly warns that the lower bound may not extend to unrestricted networks. Remark 6.3 also drops the inference that proving the conjecture must exploit powers of two.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies experimental implementation settings, hardware information, or code/data access instructions. The explicit mathematical construction and its detailed appendix verification are retained.

R1.justification: V1 positions the work around the unresolved Hertrich et al. conjecture. V2 cites Bakaev et al. [2025b] as refuting it, reporting the upper bound ceil(log_3(d−1))+1 and a two-layer construction for the five-number maximum. This substantially changes the research context. V2 also adds Bakaev et al. [2025a] on nonnegative weights and additional verification-related references.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the introduction, contribution framing, Remark 6.3, and the new Conclusion and Limitations section. Numbered introductory and preliminary subsections become unnumbered headings, and author information changes. Most mathematical exposition and appendix prose retain their wording and order.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a NeurIPS layout with a redesigned title/author block, different typography and spacing, and more compact mathematical displays throughout. V1 Figure 1a and Figures 2a–b are combined into v2 Figure 1, while v1 Figure 1b is removed. The remaining diagrams are resized and relocated, and the appendix notation table is reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the paper's framing by acknowledging the conjecture's reported refutation and explaining the substantive limitation imposed by braid-conformity in Section 7. These gains outweigh limited losses of formal clarity: the general-rank derivation remains without its statement and definition of R, and Proposition 2.3 loses a basis-function factor. With the principal results and proofs largely retained, the net improvement is limited.
